readerAnswers.news: Reuters reported on September 10 that Microsoft plans to expand its data-centre capacity from about 12 gigawatts now to about 38 gigawatts by 2032.
readerAnswers.mechanism: A gigawatt measures power: the rate at which electricity can be supplied or used at a moment.
readerAnswers.limit: It is not a reading of electricity Microsoft is consuming today, and it does not tell us how much energy those facilities would use over a day or year.

terms.data centre: Data centres are physical buildings filled with servers.
terms.gigawatt: A gigawatt measures power: the rate at which electricity can be supplied or used at a moment.

explainBack: Microsoft reportedly plans to expand data-centre power capacity from about 12 gigawatts now to about 38 by 2032. That is capacity for computing infrastructure, not a reading of energy already consumed.
unseenTransfer: If another company announces a 5-gigawatt facility plan, ask when the capacity is planned, whether it is available now and how much energy the facility would actually use over time.
repairs: Led with the reported roadmap, used about 38 consistently, defined power capacity separately from energy consumption and bound the visible Bloomberg excerpt without claiming paywalled access.
limitations: Producer review is not independent admission.
No observed human-comprehension evidence is claimed.
Microsoft did not immediately confirm the reported plan in the cited Reuters item.
